description: The commands actions/shell knows (commands.json): how each reads its arguments, and what it does when it runs. commandgen writes commands_gen.go from it; enumgen writes the CommandTrait, AttackSpelling, ArgumentReading, RequestReading and CodeReading of the $defs.

command-entry.description: One command, or one subcommand of it: its names, options and command traits, and the sources that say so.

names.description: The names it runs by. A subcommand's entry has the names of its parent.

name_pattern.description: A Go regexp a name with a version in it matches as a whole (python[0-9.]*).

subcommand.description: The words after the command that name the subcommand; the entry of the shorter list is its parent.

options.description: Before the subcommand for the command itself; after it for a subcommand.

operands.description: For a runs-operand entry: the arguments before the command it runs (the DURATION of timeout).

assignments.description: For a runs-operand entry: NAME=value words come before the command it runs (env).

operands_only.description: It reads its arguments by their number and place, not as options: an argument that begins with - is an operator or a string (test and [).

options_after_operands.description: It reads a word that begins with - as an option after its first operand too, up to -- (getopt's permutation). Without it, its options end at its first operand.

value_options_complete.description: The options declare every option of it that takes a value: an option they do not have takes none.

long_option_prefixes.description: Prefixes a long option may take and stay the same option, such as curl's --expand- (--expand-header is --header, its value expanded).

operand_request.description: For a command that sends a request: what its operands are to the request.

value_reading.description: How the command reads the value of a variable that bash expands in one of its operands as code, as a test ran the command with the value of a variable and saw the value run.

input_value_code.description: It runs as code the value of a variable that its standard input carries: a test gave it the value through a pipe, a heredoc whose delimiter is not quoted and a here-string, and saw the value run.

unsourced.description: What of the entry no source supports, kept from the tables before commands.json, and why.

value.description: It takes the next word as its value, or one joined to it.

cluster.description: Other short options may come before it in the same word (-ec for -c).

joined.description: Its value may be joined to it: -eCODE, or --eval=CODE for a long spelling.

attack.description: The spellings of the option with its value (the long spelling with = for one word) by which an attacker's word was seen to run a program.

harmless.description: The spellings by which an attacker's word was seen not to run a program.

remote.description: The program of its value runs on the remote side: by a local path or SSH, not HTTPS.

ends_options.description: After its value the command reads no option: the value is the code it runs, and the words after it are the code's arguments (-c of a shell or python).

request.description: For a command that sends a request: what the option's value is to the request.

value_reading.description: How the command reads the value of a variable that bash expands in the option's value as code, as a test ran the command with the value of a variable and saw the value run.

command-trait.description: What a command does when it runs.

oneOf.description: It runs the words after its options as a command, or passes them to a shell.
It reads its arguments as bash code or arithmetic.
It reads its arguments as names of variables, whose subscripts are arithmetic.
It reads its standard input as code, or as commands to run.
The program it runs is decided by files of the git directory (.git) of the repository: hooks and configuration (core.hooksPath, core.fsmonitor).
It writes to GitHub with the GitHub token.
It sends data to a host its arguments name.
It runs the command after it as a process that may outlive the step.
It writes a value made from its standard input, a here-string or heredoc, or its operands: the value is changed or cut, not copied whole.
It writes a digest or a count of its input, which does not give the input back.

attack-spelling.description: How an attacker writes an option with its value.

oneOf.description: One word with blanks in it: a value inside quotes.
One word with no blanks in it: the name of a branch, or a value outside quotes, which the shell splits at blanks.
The option and its value as two words, the value with no blanks: a value outside quotes that the shell splits at a blank.
One word of only ASCII letters, digits, ., - and _, a short option with its value joined to it: the name of a repository, which holds no = and no blanks.

argument-reading.description: How a command reads the value of an option; a value without one is data.

oneOf.description: The value, and the words after it, are code.
The value names a program the command runs.

request-reading.description: What a word of a command that sends a request is to the request.

oneOf.description: The URL the request goes to.
The path of an API of the command's host, or, when it holds ://, the URL the request goes to (gh api).
The host the request goes to (--hostname of gh api).
What the request carries to the host it goes to: a header, a user and password, a cookie, a body.

code-reading.description: How bash, or a program bash gives a value to, reads the value of a variable as code.

oneOf.description: An argument that the command reads as code: an operand of eval, the code of -c of a shell or of an interpreter, a program that git runs.
The command word outside quotes: bash splits the value into words, and the first word names the program that runs with the other words as its arguments.
What a command that reads its standard input as code reads: the body of a heredoc whose delimiter is not quoted, a here-string, or what a command before a pipe writes.
An arithmetic expression, or the name of a variable whose subscript is an arithmetic expression: bash evaluates a subscript of the value, and a command substitution in the subscript runs.
The transformation ${NAME@P}: bash expands the value of the variable as a prompt string, and runs a command substitution in the value.

quote.description: Words of a source pinned to a version, as the source has them.
